purpose: A bounded development smoke test of the production Insight OFF/AUTO contrast, with static knowledge cards and ordinary background assistance enabled in both arms.
evaluation_scope: DEVELOPMENT_ONLY_NOT_HOLDOUT. Questions were written with known routing vocabulary to exercise three existing packs, before observing model answers. This checks exposure and produces reviewable paired answers; it cannot establish generalization, routing recall, statistical significance, or overall product quality.
ground_truth_origin: No generated reference answer or fabricated scoring facts. Reviewers must check claims, citations and uncertainty directly against the pinned original PDFs. Empty key_facts arrays are deliberately not a completeness gold standard.

protocol.treatment: Same production service and corpus, context_assistance_enabled=true, knowledge_skill_mode=auto, insight_mode=auto. Actual complete cards may differ because Insight shares their budget; report the actual inputs.
protocol.bounds: Three pairs, six requests maximum, one repetition. Use the production task completion budget: 8192 for grounded research, 2048 for ordinary chat, with no explicit experiment cap override. Stop on provider error/incomplete response; never automatically retry. Report actual provider token usage, not estimated bytes. The run uses an 80000 reported-token soft stop, not a provider spend guarantee.
protocol.quality: Blind source-grounded human review is required. Activation, keyword overlap, model self-grading and runtime checks are not proof of quality.
protocol.privacy: Public PDFs only; no customer or private documents. Question metadata and review criteria are never ingested as evidence.
protocol.generation_controls: Temperature=0.1 explicitly in both arms, matching the application default rather than reading private user settings. Provider-specific options come from the shared production sdk_chat_request_options builder. Same questions and pinned PDF bytes as v1; this is a post-failure configuration repair on development data, not a new holdout.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems

rubric.warning: Without independently authored reference facts, completeness must be reviewed against the original PDFs and task requirements; no automatic gold-completeness score is valid.

questions.question: Compare these papers on retrieval-augmented generation, graph-based retrieval and the limits of long-context evidence. Write a concise evidence-backed literature review: distinguish methods and evaluations, identify disagreement or missing comparisons, and give cautious conclusions.

Based on these papers, propose one testable research hypothesis about retrieval and long-context evidence placement. State the source-backed observation, the proposed mechanism, the strongest alternative explanation, and an experiment that could disconfirm the hypothesis.

Write an evidence-backed report comparing RAG and MemGPT for a long-term private research assistant. Separate demonstrated results from proposed transfer, identify missing direct comparisons, and state which conclusions need further experiments.
